why: EVIDENCE (from dashboard). Correctness: zero 5xx everywhere - canary 0/2476 (0.00%), stable 0/7343 (0.00%), and 0 errors in every one of the four 30s windows. No error-rate regression at all. Latency, aggregate: canary looks worse than stable (p50 62 vs 34, p95 177 vs 94, p99 218 vs 104), and that is true for each endpoint too (/browse p95 150 vs 27, /search 177 vs 59, /checkout 215 vs 103). Latency, over time: the whole gap lives in the first 30 seconds. Canary p95 by window runs 210 -> 130 -> 95 -> 94 while stable sits flat at 93 -> 94 -> 95 -> 94. By 60-90s the canary matches stable and it holds that parity for the final 60s, i.e. the last half of the test. JUDGEMENT. The shape - one freshly started pod, high p95 at t=0, monotonic decay to the stable baseline, then flat - reads as cold start (JIT/class loading, cold caches, connection-pool and TLS-session fill) rather than a real performance regression. A genuine regression from a code change would persist or worsen across windows; this one fully resolves and stays resolved. The bad-looking per-endpoint aggregates are consistent with this: they are averaged over the entire 120s including the slow warm-up window, so the early spike is baked into them. The dashboard does not break endpoints down per window, so that is inference from the aggregate time series, not a measured per-endpoint steady-state number. DECISION. Steady-state latency is at parity with stable and the error rate is zero, including on /checkout, the revenue path. The release-blocking cost of a needless rollback is not justified by a transient that has already cleared. Promote. CAVEATS / CONDITIONS. (1) Sample is one canary pod and 2476 requests at 25% traffic; this does not exercise 1.1 at full load, so it cannot rule out a capacity or saturation problem that only appears at 100%. (2) The warm-up penalty is real and will recur on every new 1.1 pod, so expect a p95 bump during the rollout itself - roll out gradually (surge one pod at a time) rather than all at once. (3) Mitigate with a readiness probe that does not admit traffic until the pod is warm, or a pre-warm hit on startup. (4) Keep the 1.0 ReplicaSet available and watch p95 and 5xx through the rollout; roll back if elevated latency persists past the first ~60s of a new pod's life or if any 5xx appear.
